  "evidence_refs": ["Original request S1", "Original request S2"],
  "headline": "Intake established the endpoint change and discovery questions.",
  "outcome": "done",
  "summary": "S1 — Fact: the repository is an existing Node.js project with an in-memory user store and an HTTP server at src/server.js; README.md describes it. Discovery source hints, not yet verified: README.md, src/server.js, the store implementation, package metadata, and existing tests. Discovery must establish the route, store behavior, runtime capabilities, and test commands before implementation choices can be made. Assumption: the isolated source checkout remains at its snapshot until the final return. S2 — Outcome: add name filtering and pagination, with tests, to the existing user list endpoint; the change must be usable by that endpoint’s HTTP clients. Discovery must first establish the existing API conventions and data model, then resolve filter matching, pagination parameters, defaults, ordering, response shape, and invalid-input behavior; these answers block the endpoint contract and its tests. Discovery must also establish how the runtime identifies callers, what user data is shared or hidden, and the store’s lifetime and reset behavior; these answers block assessment of interaction and state effects. Recorded default: preserve existing identity, visibility, sharing, lifetime, and persistence behavior, ruling out new authentication, session handling, and durable storage. Tests can show the result during verification; the source change becomes visible in the returned checkout at final return, and a deployed endpoint reflects it only after release."
